excerpt: Splash makes a music-making game on Roblox, a beat-making app and the Wemixed remix site. Formerly Popgun, it raised a $20.8M Series A in 2021.
content:
Splash is a music technology company that builds games and tools for making music, aimed mainly at young creators. Its best-known product is Splash on Roblox, which the company calls the biggest music stage on Roblox: players skate, dance, make music with sound packs and perform live to other players in virtual clubs. Splash also has a stand-alone app with a library of sound packs and a beat-maker instrument, and Wemixed, a web platform where people make short mixes in seconds and build on each other's tracks. The company says it develops its own audio technology, including AI-powered virtual instruments, and it has created a virtual artist character called Kai.

PocketGamer.biz reported that Splash was founded in 2017 under the name Popgun and that Stephen Phillips was its CEO in 2021. Business News Australia described it as an Australian company. In 2021 PocketGamer.biz said the Roblox game had about 10 million monthly active users and that more than 7.8 million people had made music in it.

Funding

In November 2021 Splash announced a Series A of about $20.8 million co-led by Amazon's Alexa Fund and BITKRAFT Ventures, with Khosla Ventures and King River Capital, according to PocketGamer.biz and Digital Music News. Business News Australia reported the round as A$27 million. Splash said the money would go into AI-powered virtual instruments, community growth, partnerships and new venues in the game.

Pricing

Splash does not publish a price list on its website. The game is played inside Roblox, where any in-game purchases are shown, and Wemixed and the app are reached from Splash's site.

Who it suits

Splash suits teenagers and casual creators who want to make and share music in a game-like setting without learning a full music production program. Producers who need professional mixing tools will want a digital audio workstation instead.

We have not tested Splash. This page is based on the Splash website and on PocketGamer.biz, Digital Music News and Business News Australia.
